speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Law (a) whether proceedings can be brought under section 4 of the Community Disputes Resolution Act 2015 for cases of smoking near balconies or windows in homes when the second-hand smoke interferes with a neighbour’s enjoyment of his property; and (b) if so, what kind of evidence will need to be presented in order to show such interference.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Any evidence that points towards the source of interference, the type of interference, or its intensity and surrounding circumstances, would therefore be relevant.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: In addition, the Member would also be familiar with the approach of the Community Dispute Management Framework (CDMF), which is to encourage neighbours involved in disputes to always first attempt direct, friendly discussions between neighbours, or mediation, and only file a claim with the CDRT as a measure of last resort.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This approach emphasises communication and the building of relationships, in particular, between neighbours and recognises that a legalistic, litigious approach is not usually the best or most efficient way to resolve disputes in the community and it is certainly not the first port of call.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This approach gives parties a better chance at reaching mutually acceptable solutions in a fast and amicable manner, without escalating the dispute through the process of evidence-gathering or trading allegations, as the case might be.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: These include promoting neighbourliness as a way to reduce the likelihood of disputes arising in the first instance and also increasing the awareness and accessibility on the use of community mediation as the primary way to resolve disputes between neighbours.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think the massive number is not worrying, what is worrying is that only about 2% actually approached the Community Mediation Centre (CMC) or CDRT for help.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I ask Minister, what are we doing in terms of creating more awareness of CMC or CDRT option?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Two, how can we make the whole process easier or more accessible to members of the public?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I think, the Member has in part, answered the question himself.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: CMC is something that is available, the threshold is low, and the cost, if I am not mistaken from memory, is $5 per claim.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Sometimes, there are difficulties, of course, getting both sides to come to mediation.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, that takes care of those cases where consensual mediation might not be possible.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In addition, if the matter escalates and, despite repeated attempts, there is no possibility of a consensual or a friendly or amicable resolution, then the Member is able to advise the resident to come to the CDRT.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In that situation, obviously, the limitation is in part that there must be substantial evidence, at least substantial to the extend that you cross the relevant threshold in a manner which I have explained just now, because CDRT is an adjudicatory tribunal and it has to go on the basis of what is the appropriate remedy to impose, given the nature of the evidence.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And of course, the Act also sets out the circumstances which the tribunal will look at when considering the appropriateness of the remedy, bearing in mind that this is smoking within the confines of an individual's own home.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Obviously, you have got to find a balance between what you do in your own home and the impact that you might have on another individual trying to have a quiet enjoyment of his or her own home.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, these are the options available with the consequential challenges that might apply.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But these options will be looked at and enlarged as we review the CDMF to look at more substantial and also more practical solutions to solve these problems.
